parentIntro: Bigger addition, still by strategy rather than by column rules. Two roads she already half-knows from Week 4: SPLIT (47 + 38 → 40+30=70, 7+8=15, 70+15=85) and JUMP (47 → +30 → 77 → +8 → 85). Written columns are fine if she wants them, but only after she can say roughly what the answer should be.
watchFor: The classic wrong answer is 47 + 38 = 715 — adding each column as a separate little sum and gluing the results together. The cure is estimating FIRST: “about 50 add about 40, so around 90.” If her answer isn't near her estimate, she'll catch it herself, which is worth far more than you catching it.

demo.title: Two roads to 47 + 38
demo.say: You did this with take-aways in week four. Today the same two roads, but for adding — and the numbers are bigger.

steps.caption: estimate first — always
steps.say: Before anything, let's guess. Forty seven is nearly fifty, thirty eight is nearly forty. So the answer will be somewhere around ninety.

steps.caption: road 1: split into tens and ones
steps.say: Road one. Split both numbers up. Forty and thirty make seventy. Seven and eight make fifteen. Seventy and fifteen make eighty five.

steps.caption: road 2: jump along the number line
steps.say: Road two. Start at forty seven, jump thirty to seventy seven, then three to land on eighty, then five more. Eighty five again!

steps.caption: close to the estimate, so it's sensible
steps.say: Eighty five. And we guessed about ninety, so that feels right. Both roads, same answer.

weDo.model: Whiteboard, three lines: hundreds, tens, ones. Let her split both numbers before adding anything.
steps: Estimate first, together: “about 160 add about 130 — so around 290.”
Put them back together: 200 + 70 + 14. Ask her how to handle the 14 (it's a ten and four → 284).
Compare with the estimate — 284 against about 290. Ask: “does that feel right?”

weDo.model: Number line. Point out that 199 is desperate to be 200 — it only needs 1.
steps: Now the important question: “we added one extra to make it easy — so what do we do now?” (Give it back: 246 − 1 = 245.)
Name the trick: “round it up, then pay it back.” Try 299 + 34 together if she's enjoying it (333).
